gaps.sentence: I'll take the job ___ they don't offer me any more money.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a future possibility that will not change the decision.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: ___ she was utterly exhausted, she stayed to help clear up.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' concedes a known fact: she was exhausted and still stayed.

gaps.sentence: She looked ___ she hadn't slept for a week.
gaps.explanation: 'As though' = as if, describing how somebody appears.

gaps.sentence: ___ one misplaced comma, the essay is flawless.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from' = except for, introducing the single exception.

gaps.sentence: He spends money ___ it grew on trees.
gaps.explanation: 'As if it grew on trees' — the unreal comparison justifies the criticism.

gaps.sentence: He whispered ___ the children wouldn't hear.
gaps.explanation: 'So that + wouldn't' expresses intended (here negative) purpose.

gaps.sentence: I noted down the reference number ___ I needed it later.
gaps.hint: just in case it proved necessary
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = because it might be needed later; no purpose is intended.
